title: Coverings of a w-contractible affine are refined by clopen partitions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $D$ w-contractible [det-pe-wlocal-strict-contractible] be an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [sk-def-pe-site], and let $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ be a covering in this site. There are a finite partition $U=U'_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup U'_m$ into clopen subschemes (open subschemes [def-weil-open-immersion] whose underlying subsets are closed), indices $i_1,\dots,i_m$, and $U$-morphisms $g_k\colon U'_k\to U_{i_k}$. The empty partition is allowed when $U$ is empty.

proof.text: If $U=\varnothing$, the empty partition, with no indices or maps to choose, proves the assertion. Assume henceforth that $U$ is nonempty. By [sk-def-pe-site], the given covering in $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is an fpqc/pro-etale covering, so applying its finite affine refinement condition (equivalently [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering]) to the affine open $W=U$ gives finitely many indices $i_1,\ldots,i_r$ and affine open subschemes $V_k\subset U_{i_k}$ whose images cover $U$. Here the fibre product $U_i\times_U U$ appearing in [sk-def-pe-site] is identified with $U_i$ by its first projection, whose inverse is the pair $(\operatorname{id}_{U_i},f_i)$, where $f_i:U_i\to U$ is the given covering arrow; hence its affine opens are affine opens of $U_i$. The same covering definition says that every arrow $U_i\to U$ is weakly étale. There is no assumption that the original index set $I$ is finite, and repeated selected indices are harmless.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] form $V=\coprod_{k=1}^r V_k$ with its open-and-closed, pairwise disjoint components and the unique map $p:V\to U$ restricting to the given $V_k\to U$. By clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], this finite disjoint union of affine schemes is affine, so write $V=\operatorname{Spec}E$. The map $p$ is surjective: every point of $U$ is in the image of one of the $V_k\to U$, and each of these maps factors through $p$.

proof.text: Each inclusion $V_k\hookrightarrow U_{i_k}$ is étale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], hence weakly étale by clause (1) of [det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison]. Its composite $V_k\to U$ is weakly étale by composition stability in [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]. The components $V_k$ form a Zariski open cover of $V$, so source locality in the same stability statement implies that $p:V\to U$ is weakly étale. Apply clause (4) of [det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison] to these entire affine charts: the ring map $D\to E$ and its multiplication $E\otimes_D E\to E$ are flat. Thus $D\to E$ is weakly étale in the ring sense and is flat. Since $p$ is surjective, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] makes $D\to E$ faithfully flat.

proof.text: The ring $D$ is w-contractible by hypothesis, and step 3 verifies both faithful flatness and weak étaleness of $D\to E$. Apply [det-pe-wcb-split-cover] to obtain a section $s:U\to V$ satisfying $p\circ s=\operatorname{id}_U$.

source.place: Tag 098F, lemma-w-contractible-proetale-cover, proof of (1) implies (2), expanded as in the current blueprint proof

proof.text: For each component set $U'_k=s^{-1}(V_k)$ with its open subscheme structure. Continuity of $s$ and closedness of $V_k$ make $U'_k$ closed as well as open. Because the component subsets are pairwise disjoint with union $V$, their inverse images are pairwise disjoint with union $U$. On $U'_k$ the map on spaces of $s$ lands in $V_k$, and restricting its structure-sheaf map to these open subschemes gives $s_k:U'_k\to V_k$; the maps on stalks are those of $s$, so they remain local. Thus $s_k$ is a scheme morphism; define $g_k$ as $s_k$ followed by $V_k\hookrightarrow U_{i_k}$. Its composite with $U_{i_k}\to U$ is $(p\circ s)|_{U'_k}$, the inclusion $U'_k\hookrightarrow U$, so it is a $U$-morphism. Discard the empty inverse images and reindex the remaining finite family. This gives exactly the asserted partition and maps.
